User guide

The morpher

A morpher is an event on a morph track that changes the events under it for as long as it lasts — an adjustment layer for both picture and sound.

  • Targets. A morpher acts on everything below its row by default. It can also act on a frozen list of events, on named range markers, or on named areas.
  • FX batch. Its chain starts with a violet source slot, followed by the effects it adds to every target. Video and audio effects share one strip.
  • Source. It can swap the targets' source for another file, or shift their source-in.
  • Strength and fades. Strength mixes the batch in. The in and out fades ramp it at the morpher's edges.
  • Timed. Ties the batch to the morpher's own time instead of each event's.
  • Bake the FX batch writes the result into the events and removes the morpher.

Right-click a morph track and choose Add morpher here. If there is no morph track yet, use Add a Morph track in a track header's menu. Double-click the morpher to open this editor.

The probe command of kt-cli lists the effective events after morph layers. It is the quickest way to find out why something plays the way it does.
